OTT-play Native for Android is published by %1$s, part of the open-ott-play project. For privacy, support and data deletion requests, contact %2$s. Before sending material to support, remove passwords, tokens, settings files and other confidential information.

OTT-play Native for Android plays your playlists and IPTV sources. The app does not sell subscriptions, create its own user accounts or provide a commercial catalogue. The built-in demo is a synthetic video that works offline. Use only content and credentials you are lawfully permitted to access.

You can enter a source name and address, provider username and password, a MAC address registered with that provider, a programme guide address and HTTP headers. You enter the MAC address yourself; the app does not read the hardware MAC address of your device. When you choose a file, the system picker grants access to the selected playlist or settings file.

To load a catalogue and play content, the app connects to your specified provider and addresses from its catalogue or your playlist. Servers may receive required usernames, passwords, tokens, headers, the entered MAC address and information about the requested content. As with any network connection, the recipient sees the connection IP address. Logos and artwork load from catalogue addresses. These servers may have their own data retention and usage policies.

This version supports both HTTPS and unencrypted HTTP sources. HTTP does not protect transmitted passwords, tokens, addresses or viewing data from network participants. Use HTTPS, especially for sources with credentials. Encryption on your device does not protect HTTP traffic.

This version allows only HTTPS for network sources, video streams, guides, images and licence servers. Unencrypted HTTP addresses and HTTPS-to-HTTP redirects are blocked. Connection encryption protects data in transit, but the intended server receives the data it needs in readable form.

The app downloads XMLTV guides from source or playlist addresses. After sources are added, Android also schedules guide updates approximately every six hours on an unmetered network; updates may run while the app screen is closed. Android may defer them. Removing a source stops its future updates. On a phone, enabled background playback continues contacting the current stream server until you stop playback.

If selected content requires DRM, Android and the player may contact the source licence server and the device DRM provisioning server. These servers receive the requests needed to check playback entitlement and operate DRM. Licence server headers are separate from stream headers and are not sent to the device provisioning server. The app does not grant viewing rights or extract DRM keys.

Source settings and saved catalogue entries, including stream and guide addresses, are encrypted with AES-GCM and an Android Keystore key. Programme guides, favourites and resume positions are stored locally in private app storage. The app excludes its data from automatic Android cloud backups and transfers to another device.

Export happens only at your request, to a location selected in the system picker. It creates an unencrypted JSON file containing source addresses, passwords and other credentials, favourites and playback positions. Do not share it with others. If you choose cloud storage, that service processes the saved file under its own policies. Encryption of local app storage does not protect the exported file.

In Sources, you can remove a source with its saved credentials, catalogue and programme guide. Local favourite identifiers and playback positions may remain until app data is cleared. To delete all local data, clear app storage in Android settings or uninstall the app. Delete exported files separately. These actions do not delete a provider account or data held by the provider; contact the provider directly.

The app has no advertising, advertising SDKs or analytics SDKs. It does not send separate telemetry, viewing history or crash reports to the publisher. Android and Google Play system diagnostics depend on device settings and those services’ policies. App error messages are not intended to disclose passwords or tokens.

Playback uses network access, a media service and a wake lock. The current title and artwork may appear in system media controls and on the lock screen according to Android settings. Normal viewing does not require location, camera, microphone, contacts or full media library permissions. Emails you send to support are not deleted when app data is cleared; contact the publisher to request their deletion. Third-party service data is governed by that service’s policies and deletion options.
